svg.aria-label: Azure Virtual WAN hubs and connectivity: what Microsoft manages, the Basic and Standard split, the immutable hub address space, the hub router and its capacity limits, and the costs and capability the managed hub adds
svg.title: Virtual WAN is hub-and-spoke with the operations removed, and several decisions become fixed at creation — starting with an address space that can never be changed
svg.text: Microsoft owns the hub — so several fields stop being adjustable, and one never changes
WHAT MICROSOFT MANAGES
A virtual hub is a MICROSOFT-MANAGED virtual network — the core of your network in a region.
You connect a site to the HUB, not to a VNet. Traffic always goes through the hub gateway, so your
VNets do not need their own virtual network gateway. A hub gateway is NOT a virtual network gateway.
Multiple hubs per region · all hubs in a Standard WAN meshed AUTOMATICALLY · one VNet → exactly ONE hub
Separate Virtual WANs are isolated: they cannot share a hub and their hubs never communicate.
BASIC IS ONE FEATURE, AND THE UPGRADE IS ONE-WAY
Basic
site-to-site VPN ONLY. Cannot adjust gateway scale units for throughput.
Standard
ExpressRoute · User VPN (P2S) · S2S VPN · inter-hub and VNet-to-VNet
transit through the hub · Azure Firewall · NVA in a virtual WAN
You can upgrade Basic → Standard, but never revert. So the question is not “which tier” but “is S2S VPN all this will ever do”.
THE HUB ADDRESS SPACE CAN NEVER BE CHANGED
PREFIX
ADDRESSES
WHY
the stated minimum
recommended, for future scalability
REQUIRED if Azure Firewall runs in the hub
The hub allocates its OWN subnets from this space: hub router, ExpressRoute, S2S, P2S, Firewall, NVAs.
So a /24 hub has no room to grow a firewall into — and the field that would fix it cannot be edited.
Must not overlap other hubs in the same WAN, any on-prem range, or any connected VNet. A hand-built hub can be resized while peered; this cannot.
THE HUB ROUTER — A COMPONENT THAT CAN BE ABSENT, AND CEILINGS YOU CANNOT BUY PAST
Transit between VNets exists because a ROUTER is instantiated in every hub at creation. Four statuses:
Provisioned · Provisioning ·
None
(never provisioned — Basic WAN, or a hub older than the feature)
Failed
(repaired with a Reset Router button). A hub you INHERITED is worth checking.
Routing infrastructure units
default 2 = 3 Gbps + 2,000 VMs · rises by 1 Gbps and 1,000 VMs
per unit · maximum 50 = 50 Gbps + 50,000 VMs
Units 2 AND 3 both give 3 Gbps — the first increment buys VMs, not bandwidth.
Regardless of units deployed, a SINGLE TCP FLOW above 1.5 Gbps may degrade. So saturating a fully
scaled 50 Gbps hub takes ~33 concurrent flows. One large transfer sees 1.5 Gbps at ANY size.
And regardless of capacity, the hub accepts a maximum of 10,000 routes. Buying units does not buy routes.
Third time this series: VPN gateways, ExpressRoute gateways and now the hub router all publish an aggregate loudly and a per-flow figure elsewhere.
COST, TIMING, AND THE ONE CAPABILITY ONLY THIS MODEL HAS
The abstraction does not remove the peering bill.
You configure no peerings — and still pay
VNet peering charges in-region, global peering charges across regions.
Hub pricing applies from the moment the hub EXISTS — before any gateway is created. A hand-built
hub costs nothing until you put a gateway in it. The managed model’s value is operational, not cheaper.
Two separate dials
GATEWAY scale units raise gateway throughput. ROUTING infrastructure
units raise how many VMs the router supports. Turning up the wrong one changes nothing.
Only here: ExpressRoute traffic ENCRYPTION — encrypted transit over the circuit, without the public
internet or public IPs. Privacy AND encryption together, which neither service offers alone.
VPN-to-ExpressRoute transit assumes the Branch-to-branch flag is enabled and BGP is supported on both connections.
Autoscaling exists but will not rescue a bad floor: creation-time units are a minimum it never goes below, it is not instantaneous, a scale-out can take 25
minutes, it scales only on data the router processes, and it can affect Private Endpoint connectivity. Size the minimum to the real workload.
Build times: 5–7 minutes for an empty hub, about 30 minutes with a gateway. Adopting the new route tables means deleting preexisting hub routes first, on every hub.
